mainKeyword: cordless hedge trimmer with battery and charger
guideTitle: Best Cordless Hedge Trimmers with Batteries and Chargers (2026)
metaTitle: Best Cordless Hedge Trimmers with Battery Kits
metaDescription: Six cordless hedge trimmers sold as complete kits with battery and charger, compared on blade, capacity and what the supplied pack really gets you through.
expertTake: The EGO 26 inch kit is the best complete package if you can afford its 56V platform, and the Greenworks 24V brushless 20 inch is the best mid-range kit. The Black+Decker 22 inch is the value pick. If your hedge is longer than a garden boundary, no single-pack kit will finish it, so plan on a spare battery.
introParagraphs: A kit that includes the battery and charger takes away the biggest unknown in a cordless purchase, but not all kits are equal. The pack in the box sets how long you can cut, and its size varies more than the blade does.
Buyers often compare blade lengths and ignore the amp-hours of the supplied battery. This guide looks at six complete kits through that lens, and at what each pack actually means for a real hedge.

products.name: EGO Power+ HT2601 26 in. Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit, 56V 2.5Ah
products.description:
EGO's trimmer is built around a carbon fiber rail, a material choice that cuts weight along the blade bar and keeps a 26 inch tool from feeling as long as it is. The dual-action steel blades are listed with a cut capacity of up to 1.2 inches, the biggest in this lineup, so it is the right kit for overgrown hedges.

The 56V platform is the reason it costs more. You get a 2.5Ah pack and a charger in the box, and the maker claims up to 60 minutes of runtime, but the pack is the same family used across the brand's mowers and blowers, so owners of other tools may already have spares. A 26 inch blade is still long: overhead work will tire you faster than with the 20 inch Greenworks.

Blade and rail care is the same as for any hedge tool, but resin on the carbon rail should be wiped away rather than scraped. Store the pack indoors, because a 56V cell stack holds more energy and punishes heat more than the small packs do. It is the strongest of the six if the budget stretches. A 26 inch blade also means a tall case or hook on the garage wall, since leaving it on the floor invites a bent rail. Fit the blade cover every time you put it away.
products.bestFor: Overgrown hedges that need the largest capacity and long reach.
pros: Up to 1.2 in. capacity is the largest here
Carbon fiber rail reduces weight along the blade
Battery and charger included in the kit
Long 26 inch blade covers tops fast

products.name: Greenworks 24V 20 in. Brushless Hedge Trimmer Kit, 2.0Ah, 1.1 in. Cut
products.description:
This is the one to look at when you want brushless efficiency without the cost of a big platform. A brushless motor drives dual-action steel blades at 4,000 strokes per minute, and the 1.1 inch capacity is far above what the 20V tools in this lineup offer, so it handles overgrown hedges rather than just trimmed ones.

The weight is the catch. At 8.46 pounds it is heavy for a 20 inch tool, and next to the Black+Decker 22 inch it asks more of your arms. The full wraparound handle helps because it lets you hold the tool at several angles, but a long session on tall hedges will tire you.

The 2.0Ah battery is modest for this kind of cutting, so expect the pack to drain faster on thick stems than on soft growth. Keep a spare if your hedge is long, and wipe sap from the blades after each session. The 24V pack is shared with the brand's other 24V tools. When the blade starts to tear instead of cut, the usual cause is dried sap, not a worn motor, so clean it before blaming the machine. A few drops of oil on the blade each time costs nothing and lengthens the life of a small motor.
products.bestFor: Overgrown hedges where capacity matters more than weight.
pros: 1.1 in. capacity on a 20 inch blade
Brushless motor at 4,000 SPM
Full wraparound handle for several angles
Battery and charger included
cons: 8.46 lb is heavy for the blade length
2.0Ah pack drains fast on thick stems

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX 22 in. Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit

specList.label: Area claim
specList.value: Up to 3,000 sq ft of hedge per charge

products.description:
The simplest complete kit here is also the most widely sold. A 22 inch dual-action blade cuts to 3/4 inch, and the maker claims it can trim up to 3,000 square feet of actual hedge on one charge, which is a useful way to think about runtime because it ties battery life to area, not minutes.

It does not have a brushless motor, so it is less efficient than the Greenworks and the EGO, and it cuts at a lower capacity than both. What it offers is a low price, a light body and a battery platform used across the brand's tools. For ordinary garden hedges that are cut regularly, it does the job.

Over several seasons the pack is the part that will age first, so store it indoors at part charge and buy a spare if you outgrow the single battery. Wipe the blade after use and check that the guard bar has not been bent by a stray wire.
products.bestFor: Regularly trimmed garden hedges on a modest budget.
pros: Dual-action blade keeps vibration lower
Area-per-charge claim is easy to plan with
Light enough for most gardeners
Common platform with easy spare packs

products.name: Sun Joe 24V-HT18-LTE 24V IONMAX 18 in. Hedge Trimmer Kit, 2.0Ah
products.description:
Sun Joe sells this as a compact kit with a 2.0Ah battery and charger, and the key figure is the 0.6 inch cut capacity. That is lower than every other kit here, so it is a tool for green growth and shaping rather than for cutting back old stems. The 250 watt motor spins up to 2,800 RPM, and the rust-resistant 18 inch dual-action blades are a sensible size for a small hedge.

Its value is in the size. An 18 inch blade is easy to control, and it is a good first trimmer for someone who does not want to carry a long machine. Next to the Black+Decker 22 inch, it covers less ground and cuts thinner stems, so pick it only if your hedge is small.

Care is the same as for the others, with oiling after use and indoor battery storage. The 24V IONMAX pack is shared with the brand's other tools.
products.bestFor: Small hedges and shrubs that are trimmed often.
pros: 18 inch blade is easy to steer
250 W motor with up to 2,800 RPM
Rust-resistant blades
Kit includes battery and charger
cons: 0.6 in. capacity is the lowest here

products.name: Craftsman V20 20 in. Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit with 1.5Ah Battery
products.description:
The Craftsman V20 kit is a middle-of-the-road handheld on a platform with a lot of other tools. A 20 inch dual-action steel blade is a reasonable middle length, and a rechargeable 1.5Ah battery and charger are included, which keeps the entry cost down.

Its selling point is the V20 system, which also powers the brand's drills and outdoor tools, so a shop that already runs V20 can add this one without a new battery. The pack is the smallest in this lineup, though, so runtime is short on dense hedge, and you will want a second pack for anything beyond a modest garden.

It does not stand out on capacity or power, and the listing does not highlight a brushless motor. Treat it as a platform tool, buy it if you already own V20 batteries, and keep it clean like any other trimmer. If you do not own V20 tools, the Black+Decker or Greenworks kits offer more cutting for a similar spend. Used with spare packs it becomes a perfectly serviceable weekend tool for a small suburban garden.
products.bestFor: Existing Craftsman V20 owners who want a hedge trimmer.
pros: 20 inch blade is a balanced length
Runs on the common V20 pack
Battery and charger are in the kit
Dual-action steel blade

products.name: Endutools Plus 20 in. 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 270 Degree Handle, 2 x 2.0Ah
products.description:
What makes this kit different is the rotating rear handle, which turns 135 degrees left and 135 degrees right so you can cut vertical sides without twisting your wrist. It also comes with two 2.0Ah 21V batteries and a charger, so you can swap and keep cutting, and the 20 inch dual-action blade is made of 65Mn steel.

It runs at 2,700 strokes per minute, which is a mid-range speed, and the maker claims up to 60 minutes of continuous work on two packs. As with any such figure, dense growth will cut that down. The tool is sold under a smaller brand, so parts and warranty support are thinner than for the Craftsman or Black+Decker.

For the cost, the rotating handle and the second pack are the genuine benefits. Check that the handle lock engages firmly every time, and clean the blade after each use. If the handle ever develops play, stop using it until the lock is repaired, since a loose rotating grip is the one failure on this design that affects safety.
products.bestFor: Cutting vertical sides and awkward corners with less wrist twist.
pros: 270 degree handle rotation reduces wrist strain
Two 2.0Ah batteries in the kit
65Mn steel dual-action blade
Rated up to 2,700 SPM
cons: Smaller brand with thinner parts support
Rotating handle adds a mechanism to maintain

buyingCriteria.explanation: The battery in the box sets runtime. The Craftsman ships with 1.5Ah, the Greenworks and Sun Joe with 2.0Ah and the EGO with 2.5Ah at 56V, so the EGO stores far more energy. A kit with two packs, like the Endutools Plus, lets you keep working while one charges.

Cut capacity is the stem size the blade gap will take. The EGO lists up to 1.2 inches, the Greenworks 1.1 inches, the Black+Decker 3/4 inch and the Sun Joe 0.6 inches. Match this to your hedge before you look at blade length.

A brushless motor has no brushes to wear and wastes less energy. The Greenworks and EGO are the efficient choices here for heavy hedges. Brushed motors like the Black+Decker are fine for regular trimming, but they run warmer in thick growth.

The Greenworks lists 8.46 pounds with a 20 inch blade, which is heavy for its class. A 26 inch EGO blade is longer still. Longer blades cover more ground but increase tip load, so choose a shorter blade if you trim overhead.

A kit is a better deal if the battery fits other tools you own or will buy. Craftsman V20, Black+Decker 20V MAX, Sun Joe 24V and EGO 56V each serve a family of tools. Pick the platform before the trimmer.

A slow charger can leave you waiting for hours between sessions. Check that a spare pack and charger are easy to buy for the platform. The kits here all include a charger, but charging speed and spare cost differ.

specDecoder.meaning: Energy is voltage times amp-hours. A 56V 2.5Ah pack stores far more than a 20V 1.5Ah pack.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO is 56V 2.5Ah while the Craftsman is a 1.5Ah V20 pack.

specDecoder.meaning: Strokes per minute is blade speed with no load. Higher gives a finer cut on soft growth.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks is listed at 4,000 SPM and the Endutools Plus at 2,700.

specDecoder.meaning: The widest stem the teeth will take, set by tooth gap.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO is up to 1.2 inches and the Sun Joe 0.6 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: Brand estimates assume light work on a fresh pack. Dense stems and cold shorten them.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EGO and Endutools Plus both quote up to 60 minutes.

specDecoder.meaning: Weight with the battery fitted is what you feel. Distribution matters as much as the total.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks is listed at 8.46 lb.

howWeEvaluated.title: What is in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked that every pick includes a battery and charger, and compared pack sizes. The Endutools Plus has two packs while others have one. Pack size counted heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and motor
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed cut capacity and motor type. The EGO at 1.2 inches and the Greenworks at 1.1 inches scored highest, with the Sun Joe at 0.6 inches lowest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at weight, blade length and handle design. The Greenworks at 8.46 lb lost points while the rotating handle on the Endutools Plus scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform value
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how widely each battery is used and how easy spares are to find. EGO and Black+Decker packs are common, so they scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered blade care, battery storage and brand support over three years. Owner feedback patterns shaped these scores.

cards.label: One pack
cards.text: The Black+Decker, Sun Joe, Craftsman, Greenworks and EGO ship with one battery. They are cheaper and fine for short jobs, but you wait while it charges.

cards.label: Two packs
cards.text: The Endutools Plus ships with two 2.0Ah batteries. You can swap and keep going, which suits longer hedges.

howToChoose.note: Choose one pack for short jobs and two packs for hedges that take over half an hour.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a handle that rotates or a wraparound design so you can cut vertical sides without twisting your wrist. Also check that the blade head stays visible while you work.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Endutools Plus has a 270 degree rotating handle, and the Greenworks 24V has a full wraparound handle. Both cut awkward angles with less strain than a fixed grip.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your hedge is overgrown or long, which points to the EGO HT2601 or the Greenworks 24V brushless for capacity and runtime.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if your hedge is small and neat. The Sun Joe 18 inch or the Black+Decker 22 inch will do the work without extra cost.

maintenance.why: Sap hardens on the teeth and cuts capacity. Oil protects the steel.
Store packs at partial charge. A full pack in a cold shed ages faster.
Rotating handles like the Endutools Plus rely on a lock. A loose lock makes the tool feel unsafe.
Clippings clog vents and trap heat. Brush them out with the battery removed.
A bent bar causes stalling. Replace it if it will not straighten.

faq.q: Which pack size do I need?
faq.a: For a short garden hedge a 2.0Ah pack is enough. For long or thick hedges choose the EGO 56V or buy a spare, since a single small pack will not finish the job.

faq.q: Are kits better value than bare tools?
faq.a: For a first-time buyer, yes, since you get the battery and charger. If you already own batteries on the platform, a bare tool is cheaper.
They run cooler and last longer, which helps in thick growth. The Greenworks and EGO are the efficient choices here.

faq.q: How much capacity do I need?
faq.a: For regularly cut hedges, 3/4 inch is enough. For overgrown hedges, aim for 1 inch or more, as on the Greenworks 24V and EGO.

faq.q: How long does a charge last?
faq.a: Brands claim up to 60 minutes, but dense growth shortens that. Plan a spare pack for hedges that take more than 20 minutes.

faq.q: Can the same battery power other tools?
faq.a: Yes, within the same platform. EGO 56V, Craftsman V20, Black+Decker 20V MAX and Sun Joe 24V each run other tools in their range.
